rituals.title: THE BLAME PIE
rituals.name: THE BLAME PIE
rituals.hook: The Blame Pie: Personalisation gets smaller here. One job: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
rituals.recognition_cue: The Blame Pie: Personalisation gets smaller here. One job: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
rituals.goal: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
rituals.mission: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
rituals.challenge: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
rituals.immediate_need: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
rituals.game_move: Imagine A Pie opens; Check The Whole pivots. Choose Repair lands; leave it.
rituals.unique_game_move: Imagine A Pie opens; Check The Whole pivots. Choose Repair lands; leave it.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Self-blame, guilt & shame

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
The Blame Pie: Personalisation gets smaller here. One job: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.

GAME MOVE
Imagine A Pie opens; Check The Whole pivots. Choose Repair lands; leave it.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Imagine A Pie — Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
2. Share The Slices — In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Check The Whole — Make sure all slices together equal 100.
4. Find Your Slice — Focus only on your true share.
5. Choose Repair — Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.

FINISH MOVE — Let Choose Repair be enough.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
The Blame Pie proves this: owning your part is different from taking all the blame. Let Choose Repair be enough.
rituals.formula_flow: Imagine A Pie → Share The Slices → Check The Whole → Find Your Slice → Choose Repair
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Set it down if sharing turns into punishment or erases genuine accountability.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

A thought can sound true and still drive badly.

GAME MOVE
Start Picture; use Name Likely. After Select Direction, return.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Picture — Picture two arrows.
2. Make Room — One shows the next hour if you obey the thought; the other reveals what unfolds over sixty minutes when you make room for it but follow a chosen value.
3. Name Likely — Name the likely behaviour at each arrow’s end.
4. Select Direction — Select by direction, not by mental volume.

FINISH MOVE — Select Direction is your cue to stop.

WIN SIGNAL
The Life Direction Test lands here: a thought can sound true and still drive badly. Once Select Direction happens, stop.

rituals.title: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
rituals.name: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
rituals.ritual_name: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
rituals.hook: Use Close One Door For Thirty Seconds on Decision paralysis. Only this matters: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.recognition_cue: Use Close One Door For Thirty Seconds on Decision paralysis. Only this matters: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.goal: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.mission: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.challenge: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.immediate_need: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.game_move: Start Close Door; use Reopen Choice. Nothing follows Choose Next here.
rituals.unique_game_move: Start Close Door; use Reopen Choice. Nothing follows Choose Next here.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Perfectionism & performance pressure

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Use Close One Door For Thirty Seconds on Decision paralysis. Only this matters: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.

GAME MOVE
Start Close Door; use Reopen Choice. Nothing follows Choose Next here.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Close Door — Picture the two leading options. Cross out one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
2. Read Protest — Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Reopen Choice — Uncross the option. Repeat once with the other door closed so both reactions receive the same test.
4. Choose Next — Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Close One Door For Thirty Seconds lands here: a hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes. Finish there, not beyond Choose Next.
rituals.formula_flow: Close Door → Read Protest → Reopen Choice → Choose Next
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use pretend closure for urgent, coercive, unsafe, or irreversible choices.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

GAME MOVE
Start Ask Quality; use Look Single. Stopping line: Let Certainty.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Ask Quality — Ask: ‘What quality do I want this next action to carry?’ Pick one—honesty, courage, care, fairness, patience.
2. Look Single — Define how that quality would look in a single visible movement today.
3. Let Certainty — Let certainty remain absent while the compass gives direction.

FINISH MOVE — Let Certainty is your cue to stop.

rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Open Voices — Complete three lines.
2. Name Feeling — FEELING SAYS: include its full truth.
3. Name Facts — FACTS SAY: include only verified information.
4. Build Wisdom — WISE RESPONSE: honour the need in the first line and the constraints in the second.
5. Use Wisdom — Read only the third line before acting.

rituals.name: LET BREATH BREATHE YOU
rituals.hook: Let Breath Breathe You tests Observer loss directly. Aim: Remove the manager from respiration.
rituals.recognition_cue: Let Breath Breathe You tests Observer loss directly. Aim: Remove the manager from respiration.
rituals.goal: Remove the manager from respiration.
rituals.mission: Remove the manager from respiration.

rituals.unique_game_move: Use Follow Breaths; work through Start. Stop at Witness Motion.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Observer loss & cognitive fusion

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
Let Breath Breathe You tests Observer loss directly. Aim: Remove the manager from respiration.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Remove the manager from respiration.

GAME MOVE
Use Follow Breaths; work through Start. Stop at Witness Motion.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Follow Breaths — Follow three natural breaths exactly as they occur.
2. Leave Breath Alone — Do not deepen, slow, count, or improve them.
3. Start — Notice where each begins by itself and where it ends without instruction.
4. Let Body — Between breaths, let the body choose again.
5. Witness Motion — Your only action is witnessing what already knows how to move.

FINISH MOVE — Let Witness Motion be enough.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Let Breath Breathe You gives one sign: remove the manager from respiration. Stop at Witness Motion.
rituals.formula_flow: Follow Breaths → Leave Breath Alone → Start → Let Body → Witness Motion
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use outward sensory contact if breath attention increases panic or air hunger.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

1. Choose Slow — Choose a slow, comfortable pace in which inhale and exhale feel smooth.

A sustainable cadence can organise the whole system.

1. Choose Slow — Choose a slow, comfortable pace in which inhale and exhale feel smooth.
2. Use Quiet — Use a quiet timer or gentle movement as metronome, never forcing lung volume.
3. Continue Long — Continue long enough to find a repeatable rhythm, then remove the metronome and keep one easy cycle.
rituals.win_reward_source:
🏆 WIN
Rhythm Before Depth gives one sign: a sustainable cadence can organise the whole system. Leave at Continue Long.

GOAL

GAME MOVE

rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Pick Requires — Pick a count that requires no effort.
2. Count Exhale — Inhale for that count, exhale for the same count, and leave any natural pause untouched.
3. Imagine Pair — Imagine each pair forming equal sides of a bridge.
4. Complete Few — Complete a few balanced crossings, then let counting dissolve.

FINISH MOVE — Complete Complete Few, then return to your day.

The Even Bridge gives one sign: symmetry gives attention a simple crossing. End with Complete Few.

rituals.unique_game_move: Use Choose Slow; work through Return Direction. Sequence closes: Let Movement.

about 90 seconds

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Give respiration a visible partner.

GAME MOVE
Use Choose Slow; work through Return Direction. Sequence closes: Let Movement.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Slow — Choose one slow movement with two directions—arms open and close, rise and lower, reach and return.
2. Return Direction — Pair the expansive direction with inhale and the returning direction with exhale.
3. Let Movement — Let movement size follow comfort, then complete one cycle without conscious pairing.

rituals.name: WHAT SURVIVES THREE STATES?
rituals.hook: What Survives Three States? loosens Comparison distortion. Stay here: Compare experience across waking, dreaming, and dreamless sleep.
rituals.recognition_cue: What Survives Three States? loosens Comparison distortion. Stay here: Compare experience across waking, dreaming, and dreamless sleep.

rituals.unique_game_move: Take Picture Appears; keep Ask Claims literal. End when Hold Conclusions completes.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Comparison & rejection

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
What Survives Three States? loosens Comparison distortion. Stay here: Compare experience across waking, dreaming, and dreamless sleep.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Compare experience across waking, dreaming, and dreamless sleep.

GAME MOVE
Take Picture Appears; keep Ask Claims literal. End when Hold Conclusions completes.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Picture Appears — Picture what appears in waking, what appears in dreams, and what is absent or inferred in deep sleep.
2. Ask Claims — Ask which claims of identity remain supported across all three.
3. Hold Conclusions — Hold conclusions lightly; this is an inquiry into ongoing sense, not a demand for belief.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
What Survives Three States? earns its finish: compare experience across waking, dreaming, and dreamless sleep. No second proof after Hold Conclusions.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture Appears → Ask Claims → Hold Conclusions
rituals.safety:

Discontinue if sleep-related inquiry worsens insomnia or unreality.

4. Decide After — Decide only after the braid is complete.

GOAL
Equal pressure gives restless energy a shared route down.

GAME MOVE
Begin Press Equal; no side task before Step Down. End when Reach Zero completes.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Press Equal — Press palms together—or both hands into one cushion—at about twenty percent effort. Keep breathing ordinary.
2. Match Force — Adjust until neither side wins and the pressure feels equal. Hold that match for two seconds.
3. Step Down — Lower both sides together through three gentle levels: fifteen, ten, then five percent.
4. Reach Zero — Reach zero, rest both hands on a stable surface, and notice whether the urge to press returns.

rituals.hook: Replay The Turning Point At Half Speed keeps Action avoidance workable. The reset points here: Find the turning point, not another theory about the whole conversation.

rituals.unique_game_move: Keep order: Recall Exchange, then Shift. Keep Fact ends the useful part.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

HOOK
Replay The Turning Point At Half Speed keeps Action avoidance workable. The reset points here: Find the turning point, not another theory about the whole conversation.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Find the turning point, not another theory about the whole conversation.

GAME MOVE
Keep order: Recall Exchange, then Shift. Keep Fact ends the useful part.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Recall Exchange — Choose no more than ten seconds of the interaction, beginning before the moment that felt different.
2. Halve Speed — Replay it once in imagination at half speed. Keep to observable words, pauses, volume, face, and movement.
3. Shift — Stop at the first change and name it without motive: ‘the pause lengthened,’ ‘the volume rose,’ or ‘the reply shortened.’
4. Keep Fact — Keep that one fact. End the replay before building another explanation.

FINISH MOVE — Let Keep Fact be enough.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Check Replay The Turning Point At Half Speed against this: find the turning point, not another theory about the whole conversation. Have Keep Fact; move on.
rituals.formula_flow: Recall Exchange → Halve Speed → Shift → Keep Fact
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if replay raises distress, becomes compulsive, or concerns abuse or danger that requires support and protection.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

Create Memory gets first beat; Include Time is pivot. Last decision: Look Backward.

One pass: Seed Options through Play Pairs. Crown Next lands; leave it.
rituals.play_the_loop:

2. Pick Criterion — Choose one criterion that matters for this round and Picture it above the bracket. Do not switch it mid-game.
3. Play Pairs — Compare only two options at a time. Advance the one that better meets the declared criterion.
4. Crown Next — Crown the final survivor as the next option to inspect or act on—not as a permanent life verdict.

FINISH MOVE — Crown Next closes the round.

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.

GAME MOVE
Imagine A Pie opens; Check The Whole pivots. Choose Repair lands; leave it.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Imagine A Pie — Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
2. Share The Slices — In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Check The Whole — Make sure all slices together equal 100.
4. Find Your Slice — Focus only on your true share.
5. Choose Repair — Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.

FINISH MOVE — Let Choose Repair be enough.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
The Blame Pie proves this: owning your part is different from taking all the blame. Let Choose Repair be enough.
items.formula_flow: Imagine A Pie → Share The Slices → Check The Whole → Find Your Slice → Choose Repair
items.safety:
PAUSE
Set it down if sharing turns into punishment or erases genuine accountability.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

items.title: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
items.name: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
items.ritual_name: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
items.hook: Use Close One Door For Thirty Seconds on Decision paralysis. Only this matters: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
items.recognition_cue: Use Close One Door For Thirty Seconds on Decision paralysis. Only this matters: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
items.goal: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
items.mission: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
items.challenge: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
items.immediate_need: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
items.game_move: Start Close Door; use Reopen Choice. Nothing follows Choose Next here.
items.unique_game_move: Start Close Door; use Reopen Choice. Nothing follows Choose Next here.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Perfectionism & performance pressure

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Use Close One Door For Thirty Seconds on Decision paralysis. Only this matters: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.

GAME MOVE
Start Close Door; use Reopen Choice. Nothing follows Choose Next here.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Close Door — Picture the two leading options. Cross out one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
2. Read Protest — Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Reopen Choice — Uncross the option. Repeat once with the other door closed so both reactions receive the same test.
4. Choose Next — Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Close One Door For Thirty Seconds lands here: a hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes. Finish there, not beyond Choose Next.
items.formula_flow: Close Door → Read Protest → Reopen Choice → Choose Next
items.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use pretend closure for urgent, coercive, unsafe, or irreversible choices.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

TRIGGER
Perfectionism & performance pressure

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Use Close One Door For Thirty Seconds on Decision paralysis. Only this matters: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.

GOAL
A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.

GAME MOVE
Start Close Door; use Reopen Choice. Nothing follows Choose Next here.

1. Close Door — Picture the two leading options. Cross out one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
2. Read Protest — Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Reopen Choice — Uncross the option. Repeat once with the other door closed so both reactions receive the same test.
4. Choose Next — Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.

WIN SIGNAL
Close One Door For Thirty Seconds lands here: a hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes. Finish there, not beyond Choose Next.

FORMULA FLOW
Close Door → Read Protest → Reopen Choice → Choose Next

TRIGGER
Body-state misreading

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
One Drop, Not The Ocean gives Body-sensation misinterpretation a boundary. Test this: Small contact can process what flooding cannot.

GOAL
Small contact can process what flooding cannot.

GAME MOVE
Begin Choose Tiniest; hinge on Find Dose. Close with Use Less.

1. Choose Tiniest — Choose the tiniest fragment of the difficult material: one edge, colour, word, or body sensation.
2. Return Fully — Contact it briefly, then return fully to a stabilising cue.
3. Find Dose — Hold the dose that allowed recovery.
4. Use Less — Next practice uses the same or less—not an ambitious leap.

FINISH MOVE — Use Less is your cue to stop.

WIN SIGNAL
Small contact can process what flooding cannot. In One Drop, Not The Ocean, Use Less is the exit.

FORMULA FLOW
Choose Tiniest → Return Fully → Find Dose → Use Less

Learn the borders before the system crosses them.

GAME MOVE
Begin Imagine Zones; hinge on Picture Fastest. Final beat: Place Others.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Imagine Zones — Imagine three zones: TOO HIGH, WORKABLE, TOO LOW.
2. Add Earliest — Add your earliest personal signs in body, speech, attention, and behaviour.
3. Picture Fastest — Beside each outer zone, Picture the fastest safe route toward the middle.
4. Place Others — Place the Imagine a path where others can help recognise it.

FINISH MOVE — Place Others is your cue to stop.

If learn the borders before the system crosses them., Map Your Operating Window has landed. Exit after Place Others.

items.hook: Let Breath Breathe You tests Observer loss directly. Aim: Remove the manager from respiration.
items.recognition_cue: Let Breath Breathe You tests Observer loss directly. Aim: Remove the manager from respiration.
items.goal: Remove the manager from respiration.
items.mission: Remove the manager from respiration.
items.challenge: Remove the manager from respiration.

items.game_move: Use Follow Breaths; work through Start. Stop at Witness Motion.
items.unique_game_move: Use Follow Breaths; work through Start. Stop at Witness Motion.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Observer loss & cognitive fusion

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
Let Breath Breathe You tests Observer loss directly. Aim: Remove the manager from respiration.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Remove the manager from respiration.

GAME MOVE
Use Follow Breaths; work through Start. Stop at Witness Motion.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Follow Breaths — Follow three natural breaths exactly as they occur.
2. Leave Breath Alone — Do not deepen, slow, count, or improve them.
3. Start — Notice where each begins by itself and where it ends without instruction.
4. Let Body — Between breaths, let the body choose again.
5. Witness Motion — Your only action is witnessing what already knows how to move.

FINISH MOVE — Let Witness Motion be enough.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Let Breath Breathe You gives one sign: remove the manager from respiration. Stop at Witness Motion.
items.formula_flow: Follow Breaths → Leave Breath Alone → Start → Let Body → Witness Motion
items.safety:
PAUSE
Use outward sensory contact if breath attention increases panic or air hunger.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

items.unique_game_move: Use Pick Requires; work through Imagine Pair. Let Complete Few finish.
items.trigger_play_time:

Panic & body alarm

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
The Even Bridge tests Breath-control overeffort directly. Keep this aim: Symmetry gives attention a simple crossing.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Symmetry gives attention a simple crossing.

GAME MOVE
Use Pick Requires; work through Imagine Pair. Let Complete Few finish.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Pick Requires — Pick a count that requires no effort.
2. Count Exhale — Inhale for that count, exhale for the same count, and leave any natural pause untouched.
3. Imagine Pair — Imagine each pair forming equal sides of a bridge.
4. Complete Few — Complete a few balanced crossings, then let counting dissolve.

FINISH MOVE — Complete Complete Few, then return to your day.

items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

HOOK
Replay The Turning Point At Half Speed keeps Action avoidance workable. The reset points here: Find the turning point, not another theory about the whole conversation.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Find the turning point, not another theory about the whole conversation.

GAME MOVE
Keep order: Recall Exchange, then Shift. Keep Fact ends the useful part.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Recall Exchange — Choose no more than ten seconds of the interaction, beginning before the moment that felt different.
2. Halve Speed — Replay it once in imagination at half speed. Keep to observable words, pauses, volume, face, and movement.
3. Shift — Stop at the first change and name it without motive: ‘the pause lengthened,’ ‘the volume rose,’ or ‘the reply shortened.’
4. Keep Fact — Keep that one fact. End the replay before building another explanation.

FINISH MOVE — Let Keep Fact be enough.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Check Replay The Turning Point At Half Speed against this: find the turning point, not another theory about the whole conversation. Have Keep Fact; move on.
items.formula_flow: Recall Exchange → Halve Speed → Shift → Keep Fact
items.safety:
PAUSE

1. No Sentences — Imagine five boxes. Do not use full sentences.

items.hook: At Posture–mood locking, reach for Borrow One Move From The Avatar. Make this the target: Qualities become accessible when embodied by a character.

items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Panic & body alarm

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
At Posture–mood locking, reach for Borrow One Move From The Avatar. Make this the target: Qualities become accessible when embodied by a character.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Qualities become accessible when embodied by a character.

GAME MOVE
Create Figure gets first beat; Give Posture is pivot. Final beat: Borrow.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Create Figure — Create a figure who represents the needed capacity—steady, playful, discerning, brave.
2. Give Posture — Give it posture, voice, and one signature behaviour.
3. Borrow — Borrow only that behaviour for the present situation; there is no need to become the character.

FINISH MOVE — Borrow is your cue to stop.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Borrow One Move From The Avatar is useful if: qualities become accessible when embodied by a character. Take the win at Borrow.
items.formula_flow: Create Figure → Give Posture → Borrow
items.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the avatar clearly imaginary and values-consistent.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

GAME MOVE

items.play_the_loop:
1. Option — Notice every option as improving, stable, decaying, or expiring with delay.
2. Add Condition — Add the date or condition where its arrow changes.
3. Sequence — Sequence decisions around genuine expiry rather than anxiety’s false deadlines.

GOAL
Crowded choices get clearer when only two enter each round.

GAME MOVE
One pass: Seed Options through Play Pairs. Crown Next lands; leave it.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Seed Options — Picture the available options into a simple bracket. Give an unpaired option a bye rather than inventing a rival.
2. Pick Criterion — Choose one criterion that matters for this round and Picture it above the bracket. Do not switch it mid-game.
3. Play Pairs — Compare only two options at a time. Advance the one that better meets the declared criterion.
4. Crown Next — Crown the final survivor as the next option to inspect or act on—not as a permanent life verdict.

FINISH MOVE — Crown Next closes the round.
